Dr. '''Dan Thomas Major''' ({{langx|he|דן מאיור}}; born 22 March 1973) is a professor of [[chemistry]] at [[Bar Ilan University]], specializing in [[computational chemistry]].

==Biography==
Dan Major obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D]]. from the Chemistry Department at Bar-Ilan University (BIU) in 2003, followed by three years as a postdoctoral fellow at the [[University of Minnesota]] working with Prof. Jiali Gao.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Department of Chemistry {{!}} College of Science and Engineering |url=https://cse.umn.edu/chem |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=cse.umn.edu |language=en}}</ref> In 2007 he moved to the Chemistry Department at Bar-Ilan University, where he is now a full professor.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Department of Chemistry {{!}} Bar-Ilan University |url=https://ch.biu.ac.il/ |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=ch.biu.ac.il}}</ref>

==Scientific interests and publications==
Major's research focuses on computational approaches to [[computational chemistry|chemistry]], [[biochemistry]], and [[nanotechnology]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Major Research Group {{!}} Department of Chemistry BIU |url=http://www.themajorgroup.org/ |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=www.themajorgroup.org}}</ref> These include the development of [[Modeling and simulation|simulation methods]], a study of [[enzyme|enzyme reactions]] and [[protein dynamics]], understanding [[Natural product#Synthesis|natural product synthesis]], development of [[List of protein-ligand docking software|protein-ligand docking programs]], [[in silico]] design of [[Lithium-ion battery|Li-ion batteries]], and [[fuel cell]] modeling.
He develops [[Molecular modelling|classical and quantum simulation methods]], and in particular tools for studying [[enzyme catalysis]]. This includes the development of [[Path integral formulation|path-integral methods]] for the simulations of [[zero-point energy]] and [[Quantum tunnelling|tunneling effects]] in condensed phase environments,<ref name="MajorGao2007">{{cite journal|last1=Major|first1=Dan Thomas|last2=Gao|first2=Jiali|title=An Integrated Path Integral and Free-Energy Perturbation−Umbrella Sampling Method for Computing Kinetic Isotope Effects of Chemical Reactions in Solution and in Enzymes|journal=Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation|volume=3|issue=3|year=2007|pages=949–960|issn=1549-9618|doi=10.1021/ct600371k|pmid=26627415|citeseerx=10.1.1.226.3245}}</ref><ref name="MajorGao2006">{{cite journal|last1=Major|first1=Dan Thomas|last2=Gao|first2=Jiali|title=A Combined Quantum Mechanical and Molecular Mechanical Study of the Reaction Mechanism and α-Amino Acidity in Alanine Racemase|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=128|issue=50|year=2006|pages=16345–16357|issn=0002-7863|doi=10.1021/ja066334r|pmid=17165790|url=https://figshare.com/articles/journal_contribution/3040642|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name="MajorHeroux2009">{{cite journal|last1=Major|first1=D. T.|last2=Heroux|first2=A.|last3=Orville|first3=A. M.|last4=Valley|first4=M. P.|last5=Fitzpatrick|first5=P. F.|last6=Gao|first6=J.|title=Differential quantum tunneling contributions in nitroalkane oxidase catalyzed and the uncatalyzed proton transfer reaction|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|volume=106|issue=49|year=2009|pages=20734–20739|issn=0027-8424|doi=10.1073/pnas.0911416106|pmid=19926855|pmc=2791643|bibcode=2009PNAS..10620734M|doi-access=free}}</ref> methods for [[Free energy perturbation|free energy simulations]],<ref name="DoronKohen2012">{{cite journal|last1=Doron|first1=Dvir|last2=Kohen|first2=Amnon|last3=Major|first3=Dan Thomas|title=Collective Reaction Coordinate for Hybrid Quantum and Molecular Mechanics Simulations: A Case Study of the Hydride Transfer in Dihydrofolate Reductase|journal=Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation|volume=8|issue=7|year=2012|pages=2484–2496|issn=1549-9618|doi=10.1021/ct300235k|pmid=26588977}}</ref> and novel [[Docking (molecular)|docking approaches]]. The simulation tools are typically used in conjunction with [[QM/MM|hybrid Quantum Mechanics/Molecular Mechanics (QM/MM) methods]] and have been applied to a wide range of enzymes. Among his awards is Excellence in teaching<ref>[https://www1.biu.ac.il/index.php?id=18213&pt=1&pid=11240&level=0&cPath=5,25,1692,11240,18213 Bar-Ilan University Excellence in Teaching, 2017]</ref> (2016-2017); [[:he:פרס קריל|Krill Prize]]<ref>[http://www.wolffund.org.il/index.php?dir=site&page=content&cs=3040&language=eng Krill Prizes for Excellence in Scientific Research]</ref> of the [[Wolf Foundation]] (2009); [[:he:מלגת אלון|Alon Fellowship]]<ref>[https://che.org.il/?decision=%25D7%259E%25D7%259C%25D7%2592%25D7%2595%25D7%25AA-%25D7%2590%25D7%259C%25D7%2595%25D7%259F-%25D7%2590%25D7%2599%25D7%25A9%25D7%2595%25D7%25A8-%25D7%2594%25D7%25AA%25D7%25A7%25D7%25A0%25D7%2595%25D7%259F-%25D7%2595%25D7%2594%25D7%25A8%25D7%259B%25D7%2591%25D7%2599-%25D7%2594%25D7%2595%25D7%2595%25D7%25A2%25D7%2593%25D7%2595 The Council for Higher Education website]</ref> (2008-2010); [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Scholarship]] (2003-2004); Excellent young scientist from the Israeli Chemical Society<ref>[http://www.chemistry.org.il/ The Israeli Chemical Society]</ref> (2001).

==Personal life==
Dan Thomas Major is married to Laura Major, a Ph.D. in [[English Literature]] from Bar-Ilan University, who serves as the Head of the English Department at [[Achva Academic College]].<ref>[http://www.achva.ac.il/laura-major Laura Major, English Department Achva Academic College]</ref> They live in [[Yad Binyamin]] and have five children.
